claim: KV7.1 and KCNE1 together form the cardiac IKs channel
source: The voltage-gated potassium channel KV7.1 and the auxiliary subunit KCNE1 together form the cardiac IKs channel, which is a proposed target for future anti-arrhythmic drugs.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and is supported by established scientific knowledge about cardiac ion channels.

claim: The IKs channel is a proposed target for future anti-arrhythmic drugs
source: The voltage-gated potassium channel KV7.1 and the auxiliary subunit KCNE1 together form the cardiac IKs channel, which is a proposed target for future anti-arrhythmic drugs.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and reflects current research directions in the field.

claim: Polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) activate KV7.1 via an electrostatic mechanism
source: We previously showed that polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) activate KV7.1 via an electrostatic mechanism.
evidence: This claim references previous work by the authors and is supported by citation to their prior research.

claim: The activating effect of PUFAs on KV7.1 was abolished when KV7.1 was co-expressed with KCNE1
source: The activating effect was abolished when KV7.1 was co-expressed with KCNE1, as KCNE1 renders PUFAs ineffective by promoting PUFA protonation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data from previous work.

claim: KCNE1 renders PUFAs ineffective by promoting PUFA protonation
source: The activating effect was abolished when KV7.1 was co-expressed with KCNE1, as KCNE1 renders PUFAs ineffective by promoting PUFA protonation.
evidence: This mechanism is stated in the abstract and is supported by experimental data.

claim: Neutralization of negatively charged residues in the S5-P-helix loop of KV7.1 restored PUFA effects on KV7.1 co-expressed with KCNE1
source: Here, we found that neutralization of negatively charged residues in the S5-P-helix loop of KV7.1 restored PUFA effects on KV7.1 co-expressed with KCNE1 in Xenopus oocytes.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the current study supported by experimental data in Xenopus oocytes.

claim: KCNE1 moves the S5-P-helix loop of KV7.1 towards the PUFA-binding site
source: We propose that KCNE1 moves the S5-P-helix loop of KV7.1 towards the PUFA-binding site, which indirectly causes PUFA protonation, thereby reducing the effect of PUFAs on KV7.1.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanistic model based on the experimental findings.

claim: More than 300 mutations in the genes encoding for KV7.1 and KCNE1 have been found in patients with cardiac arrhythmias
source: More than 300 mutations in the genes encoding for KV7.1 and KCNE1 have been found in patients with cardiac arrhythmias (Hedley et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hedley et al., 2009.

claim: Mutations that reduce IKs currents delay repolarization of the ventricular cardiac action potential and prolong the QT interval
source: Mutations that reduce IKs currents delay repolarization of the ventricular cardiac action potential and prolong the QT interval in the electrocardiogram, referred to as Long QT syndrome (Hedley et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Hedley et al., 2009 and represents established knowledge in cardiac electrophysiology.

claim: Long QT syndrome is a known risk factor for ventricular fibrillation and sudden cardiac death
source: Long QT syndrome is a known risk factor for ventricular fibrillation and sudden cardiac death (Nerbonne and Kass, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Nerbonne and Kass, 2005 and represents established medical knowledge.

claim: Up to 30% of patients with inherited Long QT syndrome are not protected against severe cardiac events using current anti-arrhythmic treatments
source: Up to 30% of patients with inherited Long QT syndrome are not protected against severe cardiac events using current anti-arrhythmic treatments (Goldenberg et al., 2006; Priori et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Goldenberg et al., 2006 and Priori et al., 2004.

claim: Several studies have promoted the need for novel pharmacological drugs that increase or restore the function of mutated potassium channels critical for cardiomyocyte repolarization
source: Therefore, several studies have promoted the need for novel pharmacological drugs that increase or even restore the function of mutated potassium channels critical for cardiomyocyte repolarization; as these drugs could potentially be used to treat Long QT syndrome in carriers with loss-of-function potassium channel mutations (Anderson et al., 2014; Perry et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Anderson et al., 2014 and Perry et al., 2016.

claim: Several promising compounds have been found to activate the KV7.1 channel
source: Several promising compounds have been found to activate the KV7.1 channel (Busch et al., 1994; Gao et al., 2008; Mattmann et al., 2012; Salata et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published research.

claim: The effects of several KV7.1 channel activators are dramatically impaired by KCNE1
source: Unfortunately, the effects of several KV7.1 channel activators are dramatically impaired by KCNE1 (Busch et al., 1997; Gao et al., 2008; Salata et al., 1998; Yu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to published research.

claim: The activating effect of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) on the human KV7.1 channel, expressed in Xenopus oocytes, is impaired by KCNE1
source: For example, we have previously described that the activating effect of polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) on the human KV7.1 channel, expressed in Xenopus oocytes, is impaired by KCNE1 (Liin et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the authors' previous work (Liin et al., 2015b).

claim: KV7.1 is co-assembled with KCNE1 in the native IKs channel complex in the heart
source: Because KV7.1 is co-assembled with KCNE1 in the native IKs channel complex in the heart (Barhanin et al., 1996; Sanguinetti et al., 1996), KV7.1 channel activators must affect the KV7.1+KCNE1 complex (referred to as KV7.1+E1) to prevent cardiac arrhythmias, such as in Long QT syndrome.
evidence: This is supported by citations to Barhanin et al., 1996 and Sanguinetti et al., 1996.

claim: KV7.1 is a potassium channel protein composed of six membrane-spanning segments, S1-S6
source: KV7.1, the alpha subunit of the IKs channel, is a potassium channel protein composed of six membrane-spanning segments, S1-S6: Helices S1 to S4 form the peripheral voltage-sensing domains and helices S5 and S6 form the central pore domain (Figure 1A–B) (Liin et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Liin et al., 2015a and illustrated in Figure 1A-B.

claim: Helices S1 to S4 form the peripheral voltage-sensing domains of KV7.1
source: KV7.1, the alpha subunit of the IKs channel, is a potassium channel protein composed of six membrane-spanning segments, S1-S6: Helices S1 to S4 form the peripheral voltage-sensing domains and helices S5 and S6 form the central pore domain (Figure 1A–B) (Liin et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Liin et al., 2015a and illustrated in Figure 1A-B.

claim: Helices S5 and S6 form the central pore domain of KV7.1
source: KV7.1, the alpha subunit of the IKs channel, is a potassium channel protein composed of six membrane-spanning segments, S1-S6: Helices S1 to S4 form the peripheral voltage-sensing domains and helices S5 and S6 form the central pore domain (Figure 1A–B) (Liin et al., 2015a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Liin et al., 2015a and illustrated in Figure 1A-B.

claim: KCNE1 is proposed to interact with KV7.1 in the lipid-filled space between two voltage-sensing domains
source: KCNE1, a single-transmembrane protein, is proposed to interact with KV7.1 in the lipid-filled space between two voltage-sensing domains (Figure 1B) (Chung et al., 2009; Nakajo and Kubo, 2015; Xu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chung et al., 2009; Nakajo and Kubo, 2015; and Xu et al., 2013, and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: PUFAs incorporate into the outer leaflet of the cell membrane in the same lipid-filled space as KCNE1, but closer to the transmembrane segments S3 and S4
source: We have previously proposed that PUFAs incorporate into the outer leaflet of the cell membrane in the same lipid-filled space as KCNE1, but they incorporate closer than KCNE1 does to the transmembrane segments S3 and S4 (Figure 1B) (Liin et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is a proposed model from the authors' previous work (Liin et al., 2015b) and illustrated in Figure 1B.

claim: Negatively charged PUFAs, such as docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), facilitate KV7.1 channel opening by electrostatically promoting the outward movement of the positively charged S4 helix
source: In this position close to S4, negatively charged PUFAs, such as docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), facilitate KV7.1 channel opening by electrostatically promoting the outward movement of the positively charged S4 helix (Figure 1C) (Liin et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Liin et al., 2015b and illustrated in Figure 1C.

claim: DHA shifts the voltage dependence of KV7.1 channel opening toward more negative voltages
source: As the DHA is negatively charged, DHA shifts the voltage dependence of KV7.1 channel opening toward more negative voltages (Figure 1C) (Liin et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Liin et al., 2015b and illustrated in Figure 1C.

claim: The activating effect of DHA at physiological pH (pH 7.4) was abolished when KV7.1 was co-expressed with KCNE1
source: However, we previously observed that this activating effect of DHA at physiological pH (i.e. pH 7.4) was abolished when KV7.1 was co-expressed with KCNE1 to form the IKs channel complex (Liin et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Liin et al., 2015b.

claim: KCNE1 decreases the local pH at the DHA-binding site, inducing protonation of the DHA carboxyl head at pH 7.4
source: In addition, we proposed that this reduced effect is the result of KCNE1 decreasing the local pH at the DHA-binding site, inducing protonation of the DHA carboxyl head at pH 7.4 (Figure 1D) (Liin et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism from the authors' previous work (Liin et al., 2015b) and illustrated in Figure 1D.

claim: PUFA analogues with a lower pKa of the head group, which prevents protonation at physiological pH, were able to activate KV7.1+E1 at physiological pH
source: Therefore, DHA becomes uncharged and ineffective at physiological pH. As a consequence, PUFA analogues with a lower pKa of the head group, which prevents protonation at physiological pH, was able to activate KV7.1+E1 at physiological pH (Liin et al., 2016, 2015b).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Liin et al., 2016 and 2015b.

claim: The inhibiting effect of the positively charged PUFA analogue arachidonoyl amine (AA+) was potentiated by KCNE1
source: Moreover, we showed that the inhibiting effect of the positively charged PUFA analogue arachidonoyl amine (AA+) was potentiated by KCNE1, as if the decreased local pH at the PUFA-binding site further protonated the amine head of AA+ (Liin et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Liin et al., 2015b.

claim: The ability of DHA to shift the voltage dependence of KV7.1 channel opening increases as pH increases, most likely due to deprotonation of DHA at higher pH
source: We previously described that the ability of DHA to shift the voltage dependence of KV7.1 channel opening increases as pH increases, most likely due to deprotonation of DHA at higher pH (Figure 1E, dashed line) (Liin et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Liin et al., 2015b and illustrated in Figure 1E.

claim: The pH dependence of the DHA effect on KV7.1+E1 is shifted by about 1 pH unit compared to KV7.1
source: We also described that the pH dependence of the DHA effect on KV7.1+E1 is shifted by about 1 pH unit compared to KV7.1, making DHA completely protonated and ineffective on KV7.1+E1 at physiological pH (Figure 1E, compare dashed and solid lines) (Liin et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Liin et al., 2015b and illustrated in Figure 1E.

claim: The pH dependence of the DHA effect for all three KCNE1 mutants (E1/∆N2-38, E1/D39C/E43C, E1/K41C) was similar to the pH dependence of the DHA effect on WT KV7.1+E1
source: We found that the pH dependence of the DHA effect on all three constructs was similar to the pH dependence of the DHA effect on WT KV7.1+E1 (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Mutations of the extracellular N terminus of KCNE1 did not restore KV7.1-like pH dependence of the DHA effect
source: Thus, mutations of the extracellular N terminus of KCNE1 did not restore KV7.1-like pH dependence of the DHA effect, as if extracellular charged amino acids in KCNE1 are not important for protonation of DHA in KV7.1+E1.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the experimental data on KCNE1 N-terminal mutants.

claim: Cysteines introduced into the S5-P-helix loop of KV7.1 form disulfide bonds with residues in the N terminus of KCNE1
source: Xu et al. previously reported that cysteines introduced into the S5-P-helix loop of KV7.1 form disulfide bonds with residues in the N terminus of KCNE1 (Xu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Xu et al., 2013.

claim: In other KV channels, the S5-P-helix loop exerts electrostatic effects on S4 due to its close proximity
source: In other KV channels, the S5-P-helix loop exerts electrostatic effects on S4 due to its close proximity (Broomand et al., 2007; Elinder et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Broomand et al., 2007 and Elinder et al., 2016.

claim: Four of the KV7.1 mutants (E284C, D286C, E290C, E295C) showed a range of pH-response curves in-between the curves of WT KV7.1+E1 and KV7.1 alone
source: By plotting the pH dependence of the DHA effect, we found that these mutants showed a range of pH-response curves in-between the curves of WT KV7.1+E1 and KV7.1 alone (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The pH-response curve for the DHA effect on KV7.1/D301C + E1 most closely resembled the pH-response curve for the DHA effect on WT KV7.1+E1
source: The pH-response curve for the DHA effect on KV7.1/D301C + E1 most closely resembled the pH-response curve for the DHA effect on WT KV7.1+E1 (Figure 3B, blue curve).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The pH-response curve for the DHA effect on KV7.1/E290C + E1 overlapped with the pH-response curve for the DHA effect on KV7.1 alone
source: In contrast, the pH-response curve for the DHA effect on KV7.1/E290C + E1 overlapped with the pH-response curve for the DHA effect on KV7.1 alone (Figure 3B, red curve).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The apparent pKa of the DHA effect on KV7.1/E290C + E1 was close to the apparent pKa for the DHA effect on WT KV7.1
source: The apparent pKa of the DHA effect on KV7.1/E290C + E1 was close to the apparent pKa for the DHA effect on WT KV7.1 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Negatively charged residues in the S5-P-helix loop (especially E290) promote the protonation of DHA in KV7.1+E1
source: Altogether, these data suggest that negatively charged residues in the S5-P-helix loop (especially E290) promote the protonation of DHA in KV7.1+E1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on S5-P-helix loop mutants.

claim: The pH-response curve for the DHA effect on KV7.1/E290C alone closely resembled the pH-response curve for the DHA effect on WT KV7.1
source: The pH-response curve for the DHA effect on KV7.1/E290C alone closely resembled the pH-response curve for the DHA effect on WT KV7.1 (Figure 4A, compare red dashed and black dashed curves).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: E290 only promotes DHA protonation when KV7.1 is co-expressed with KCNE1
source: These findings suggest that E290 only promotes DHA protonation when KV7.1 is co-expressed with KCNE1.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the effects of E290C mutation with and without KCNE1.

claim: Modification of KV7.1/E290C + E1 with MTSES— dramatically reduced the ability of 70 µM DHA to shift V50
source: However, modification of KV7.1/E290C + E1 with MTSES— dramatically reduced the ability of 70 µM DHA to shift V50 (Figure 4D–F).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study supported by data shown in Figure 4D-F.

claim: DHA induced a similar V50 shift in both WT KV7.1+E1 and MTSES— modified KV7.1/E290C + E1 at pH 8.2
source: In addition, DHA induced a similar V50 shift in both WT KV7.1+E1 and MTSES— modified KV7.1/E290C + E1 at pH 8.2 (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study supported by data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The negative charge at position 290 is important for tuning DHA protonation
source: This data further supports the notion that the negative charge at position 290 is important for tuning DHA protonation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the MTSES modification experiments.

claim: AA+ shifts the V50 of KV7.1 and KV7.1+E1 by approximately +10 and +23 mV, respectively
source: We previously showed that AA+ shifts the V50 of KV7.1 and KV7.1+E1 by approximately +10 and +23 mV, respectively (Liin et al., 2015b), as if KCNE1-induced protonation of the amine head improves the electrostatic repulsion on the voltage sensor induced by AA+ and further prevents channel opening (Figure 4G, cartoon).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Liin et al., 2015b and illustrated in Figure 4G.

claim: Mutation of E290 caused a significant reduction in the AA+-induced V50 shift in the presence of KCNE1
source: In the presence of KCNE1, here we found that mutation of E290 caused a significant reduction in the AA+-induced V50 shift (Figure 4G, compare black and red bar).
evidence: This is a finding from the current study supported by data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The AA+ effect on KV7.1/E290C + E1 was similar to that on WT KV7.1 alone
source: The AA+ effect on KV7.1/E290C + E1 was similar to that on WT KV7.1 alone (Figure 4G, compare red and striped bar), as if primarily E290 is responsible for the improved effect of AA+ in the presence of KCNE1.
evidence: This is a finding from the current study supported by data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Negatively charged residues in the loop connecting S5 to the pore helix are important for KCNE1-induced DHA protonation
source: Our results show that negatively charged residues in the loop connecting S5 to the pore helix, but not charged residues in the extracellular part of KCNE1, are important for KCNE1-induced DHA protonation.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the experimental results of the study.

claim: Neutralization of residue E290 at the top of the turret in the S5-P-helix loop had the largest impact on DHA protonation
source: Neutralization of residue E290 at the top of the turret in the S5-P-helix loop had the largest impact on DHA protonation.
evidence: This is a conclusion from comparing the effects of different S5-P-helix loop mutations.

claim: Neutralization of E290 fully restored KV7.1-like pharmacological sensitivity of KV7.1+KCNE1 to DHA
source: Neutralization of E290 fully restored KV7.1-like pharmacological sensitivity of KV7.1+KCNE1 to DHA.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the experimental data on the E290C mutation.

claim: DHA induced a shift in V50 of KV7.1/E290C + KCNE1 at pH 7.4
source: That is, DHA induced a shift in V50 of KV7.1/E290C + KCNE1 at pH 7.4 and the pH dependence of the DHA effect was similar as for KV7.1 expressed without KCNE1.
evidence: This is a finding from the current study.

claim: Neutralization of E290 only improved the DHA effect on KV7.1 when KV7.1 was co-expressed with KCNE1
source: We further show that neutralization of E290 only improved the DHA effect on KV7.1 when KV7.1 was co-expressed with KCNE1 and that it was the negative charge at position E290 that was important for the change in PUFA effect.
evidence: This is a conclusion from comparing the effects of E290C mutation with and without KCNE1.

claim: KCNE1 indirectly promotes PUFA protonation by inducing conformational re-arrangements in the KV7.1 channel, which moves the S5-P-helix loop closer to the PUFA-binding site
source: We propose that KCNE1 indirectly promotes PUFA protonation by inducing conformational re-arrangements in the KV7.1 channel, which moves the S5-P-helix loop closer to the PUFA-binding site.
evidence: This is the proposed mechanistic model based on the experimental findings.

claim: E290 is located in the middle of the long S5-P-helix loop and may easily reach over to the putative DHA binding site
source: This hypothesis fits with the location of each tested amino acid and the size of the effect of each tested amino acid when neutralized: E290, the residue with the largest effect, is located in the middle of the long S5-P-helix loop and may easily reach over to the putative DHA binding site, whereas D301, the residue with the least effect, is in the P-helix, located far from the putative DHA-binding site (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural considerations and illustrated in Figure 5D.

claim: D301 is in the P-helix, located far from the putative DHA-binding site
source: This hypothesis fits with the location of each tested amino acid and the size of the effect of each tested amino acid when neutralized: E290, the residue with the largest effect, is located in the middle of the long S5-P-helix loop and may easily reach over to the putative DHA binding site, whereas D301, the residue with the least effect, is in the P-helix, located far from the putative DHA-binding site (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural considerations and illustrated in Figure 5D.

claim: In a recently published cryo electron-microscopy structure of Xenopus KV7.1, the S5-P-helix loop forms a negatively charged cap above the pore domain
source: In a recently published cryo electron-microscopy structure of Xenopus KV7.1, the S5-P-helix loop forms a negatively charged cap above the pore domain (Sun and MacKinnon, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sun and MacKinnon, 2017.

claim: S280 in Xenopus KV7.1 (which corresponds to E290 in human KV7.1) reaches all the way to the ion-conducting pore
source: Especially S280 (which corresponds to E290 in human KV7.1) reaches all the way to the ion-conducting pore (Sun and MacKinnon, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sun and MacKinnon, 2017.

claim: Cysteines introduced in the S5-P-helix loop of KV7.1 (at positions 284, 286, 290, or 295) form disulfide bonds with cysteines introduced at positions 32 and 33 in the N terminus of KCNE1
source: When KV7.1 was co-expressed with KCNE1, Xu et al. reported that cysteines introduced in the S5-P-helix loop of KV7.1 (at positions 284, 286, 290, or 295) form disulfide bonds with cysteines introduced at positions 32 and 33 in the N terminus of KCNE1 (Xu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Xu et al., 2013.

claim: Cysteines introduced in the S5-P-helix loop of KV7.1 (at positions 284, 285, or 286) may form disulfide bonds with cysteines introduced at positions 40–43 in the N terminus of KCNE1
source: Chung et al. reported that cysteines introduced in the S5-P-helix loop of KV7.1 (at positions 284, 285, or 286) may form disulfide bonds also with cysteines introduced at positions 40–43 in the very end of the N terminus of KCNE1 connecting to the transmembrane segment of KCNE1, especially for KV7.1/E284C – E1/E43C and KV7.1/D286C – E1/G40C (Chung et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chung et al., 2009.

claim: Y46 in the outermost end of the transmembrane segment of KCNE1 was found in molecular dynamics simulations to dynamically interact with residues G297-D301 in the S5-P-helix loop of KV7.1
source: In addition, Y46 in the outermost end of the transmembrane segment of KCNE1 was found in molecular dynamics simulations to dynamically interact with residues G297-D301 in the S5-P-helix loop of KV7.1 (Xu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Xu et al., 2013.

claim: The S5-P-helix loop can reach all the way to KCNE1 in the lipid-filled space between neighboring voltage-sensing domains
source: These observations suggest that the S5-P-helix loop can reach all the way to KCNE1 in the lipid-filled space between neighboring voltage-sensing domains, a finding that agrees with our proposed model (schematically illustrated in Figure 5B).
evidence: This is an inference based on cited structural studies and illustrated in Figure 5B.

claim: It is insufficient to remove the N-terminal KCNE1 residues or to neutralize charged residues in the N-terminus of KCNE1 to restore KV7.1-like pH dependence of the DHA effect
source: It is, however, insufficient to remove the N-terminal KCNE1 residues, as in our KCNE1/∆N2-38 construct, or to neutralize charged residues in the N-terminus of KCNE1 to restore KV7.1-like pH dependence of the DHA effect.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the experimental data on KCNE1 N-terminal mutants.

claim: The binding of the KCNE1 transmembrane segment to the transmembrane segments of KV7.1 induces a re-arrangement of KV7.1, which moves the top of the turret closer to the PUFA binding site
source: Instead, we propose that the binding of the KCNE1 transmembrane segment to the transmembrane segments of KV7.1 induces a re-arrangement of KV7.1, which moves the top of the turret (the S5-P-helix loop) and its acidic residues closer to the PUFA binding site; therefore these acidic residues in the S5-P-helix loop promote PUFA protonation.
evidence: This is the proposed mechanistic model based on the experimental findings.

claim: ML277, ZnPy, and R-L3 activate KV7.1, but the effect is reduced by KCNE1 co-expression
source: For example, ML277, ZnPy, and R-L3 activate KV7.1, but the effect is reduced by KCNE1 co-expression (Gao et al., 2008; Salata et al., 1998; Yu et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: The proposed mechanism for the reduced sensitivity in KV7.1+E1 channels to ML277, ZnPy, and R-L3 is that KCNE1 and the compound compete for the same overall binding site or that KCNE1 blocks the access to the compound binding site
source: The proposed mechanism for the reduced sensitivity in KV7.1+E1 channels to these compounds is that KCNE1 and the compound compete for the same overall binding site (Gao et al., 2008; Seebohm et al., 2003) or that KCNE1 blocks the access to the compound binding site (Xu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published research.

claim: Mefenamic acid and DIDS have effects on KV7.1 expressed alone smaller than on KV7.1 co-expressed with KCNE1
source: In contrast, mefenamic acid and DIDS (4,4´-diisothiocyanatostilbene-2,2´-disulfonic acid) have effects on KV7.1 expressed alone smaller than on KV7.1 co-expressed with KCNE1 (Busch et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Busch et al., 1997.

claim: For DIDS and mefenamic acid, amino acids at the top of the KCNE1 transmembrane segment (KCNE1 amino acid 39–43) are important for the effect
source: For DIDS and mefenamic acid, amino acids at the top of the KCNE1 transmembrane segment (KCNE1 amino acid 39–43) are important for the effect, but there is no clear mechanism for how KCNE1 increases the effect of mefenamic acid and DIDS (Abitbol et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Abitbol et al., 1999.

claim: KCNE1 can impair or promote the effect of KV7.1 channel activators through diverse mechanisms
source: Altogether, it is clear that KCNE1 can impair or promote the effect of KV7.1 channel activators through diverse mechanisms.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the discussion of various compounds and their interactions with KCNE1.

claim: A detailed mechanistic understanding of how KCNE1 impairs the sensitivity of KV7.1 to activators will enable rational drug design of compounds that circumvent KCNE1-induced impairment
source: A detailed mechanistic understanding of how KCNE1 impairs the sensitivity of KV7.1 to activators will enable rational drug design of compounds that circumvent KCNE1-induced impairment.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential applications of the research.

claim: A mechanistic framework for the design of IKs channel activators may open up new avenues for treating cardiac arrhythmias, such as Long QT syndrome
source: A mechanistic framework for the design of IKs channel activators may open up new avenues for treating cardiac arrhythmias, such as Long QT syndrome.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential clinical applications of the research.

claim: Xenopus oocytes were surgically isolated at Linköping University or purchased from EcoCyte Bioscience
source: Xenopus oocytes were surgically isolated at Linköping University or purchased from EcoCyte Bioscience (Castrop-Rauxel, Germany).
evidence: This is a methodological detail stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Animal experiments were approved by the local ethics committee
source: Animal experiments were uppriven by the local ethics committee.
evidence: This is a statement about ethical approval in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Each oocyte was injected with 50 ng KV7.1 RNA for expression of KV7.1 alone or 25 ng KV7.1 RNA and 8 ng KCNE1 RNA for co-expression of KV7.1+E1
source: Isolated Xenopus oocytes were injected with 50 nl RNA (each oocyte injected with 50 ng KV7.1 RNA for expression of KV7.1 alone or 25 ng KV7.1 RNA and 8 ng KCNE1 RNA for co-expression of KV7.1+E1).
